title: sharp-review findings JSON
description: One review run's merged result: printed by post-review.js --sink stdout and produced by every executor of the method. VERSIONING: schema_version is method.json's schema_version; a reader refuses a version it does not know, by name, and never guesses. Any change a reader of the old version would misread (a renamed or removed field, a new status, a changed id format) bumps it.

profiles.description: The profile keys that ran, in reviewer order.

provider.description: The provider that ran it, or was requested and could not.

status.description: ok: returned a findings array ([] is a clean pass). exhausted | auth | rate_limit | timeout: the provider failed with that kind. unsupported: the run mode cannot execute this reviewer's call mode, or the provider refused the request kind. unavailable: the requested provider is not available here, no result came back, the failure had no known kind, or codex returned only its '(no findings ...)' placeholder. skipped: nothing for this profile to review (e.g. an empty diff).

dropped_findings.description: Findings this reviewer returned that failed method/finding.schema.json.

error.description: Why this reviewer has no findings: the failed call's recorded error text (never a key), else the method's reason for its status (method.json reviewer_status.error). Required for every status but ok and skipped; forbidden for ok.

reviewers.description: Every planned reviewer, in plan order. Only ok reviewers contribute findings.

confidence.description: The first method.json merge.confidence label whose min_reviewers the distinct reviewer count meets.

reviewers.description: Every reviewer that reported this finding, with its provider, in first-seen order.

principles.description: Never empty: the union of the principle ids (method principles.json) every reviewer of this finding tagged, in first-seen order; absent when none did (method.json merge.union).

findings.description: Deduplicated across reviewers by method.json merge.dedup_key, in first-seen order.
